task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: effect of preceding play on subsequent play outcome
measurement reliability of play type labels
confounding by game context and defensive matchup
sequencing and temporal dependence in play-by-play data

historical_evidence.finding: Defensive scheme change within game and across games (inferred labels) was untestable due to label or classification error. Transition matrices near-uniform and inferred label error prevented distinguishing real defense adjustments.
Play-type label backfill verification found substantial label error (e.g., PULL_UP label distribution errors). PPP for PNR passed, but team identity failed, indicating label noise.
Observed on-ball defensive scheme labels were untestable because labeling rates were too low (14.9% for DROP, 3.3% for ORL). Small sample and label error limited inference.

Play-type PPP differences were found to be artifacts of foul leakage: OTHER PPP inflated by foul rate, DRIVE PPP below foul benchmark, and only 0.7% of possessions mapped to a real play type via initiation_type.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Assessing defensive scheme change via inferred labels
failed_approaches.why: Label or classification error prevented accurate measurement (RISK:LABEL_ERROR).
Label or classification error, with team identity failing (RISK:LABEL_ERROR).
Label error and small sample size (RISK:LABEL_ERROR; RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring PPP differences from play types

evidence_establishes: Labeling of play types in the NBA PBP data is noisy and may be biased, especially for DRIVE and PNR. PPP differences can be inflated by foul leakage or mislabeling. Defensive scheme labels derived from PBP are unreliable due to low labeling rates.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP. No prior study directly tested this causal sequence with reliable labeling.
own_inferences: The data's play-type labeling is insufficiently reliable to support a causal inference about drive‑preceded pick‑and‑roll PPP. Any analysis would require either a validated labeling method or a design that can mitigate label error.
uncertainties: True accuracy of DRIVE and PNR labels; prevalence of mislabeled possessions; potential confounding by defensive matchup and game context; whether a large enough clean sample can be identified.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved evidence demonstrates high rates of label error and artifacts that undermine reliable measurement of the key variables, leading to a decision not to proceed.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type labeling is unreliable, leading to misclassification.
Potential confounding by defensive strategy and game context.
Measurement of PPP may be biased by foul leakage.

prior_work.summary: Previous studies examined labeling accuracy and defensive scheme inference, but none directly addressed whether a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises the PPP of that PNR.

risks.text: Play-type labels are noisy and may misclassify DRIVE and PNR possessions.
Defensive matchup and game context could confound the relationship.
PPP may be inflated or deflated due to foul leakage or other measurement artifacts.

design.estimand: Effect of a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR on the PPP of that PNR possession
design.sample: All possessions where a DRIVE is immediately followed by a PNR by the same or different teammate
design.power: Not feasible with current labeling; would require >80% power, but label error reduces effective sample
design.controls: Prior play type, defensive matchup, game context (score margin, period), player fatigue
design.falsification: Test the same relationship using random preceding plays (e.g., a PASS preceding a PNR) to see if any effect appears
design.multiplicity: Apply Bonferroni or FDR correction for multiple sequence types tested
design.decision_rule: Reject null if p<0.05 after correction, but only after validating labels on a subsample via manual review
design.data_version: NBA 2022‑23 to 2025‑26 regular season and playoffs (complete through 2026‑04‑13)
